context: Gantt chart with edge-bundled dependency chains — a data visualization showing a project timeline across 4 phases (~50 tasks) with hover-activated dependency tracing
first_impression: Clean, structured Gantt with a deliberate colorblind-safe palette and subtle phasing, though the visualization's core edge-bundling feature is nearly invisible in the resting state.
what_works: Paul Tol palette (blue/pink/green/yellow-green) is a purposeful, colorblind-safe choice well above schemeCategory10 defaults; typographic hierarchy is genuine — bold 17px title, quieter 12px subtitle, 10px axis ticks, 9px task labels — and the hover interaction is sophisticated, dimming non-chain elements and revealing dependency paths in accent pink.
what_doesnt: The dependency edges at rest (stroke-opacity 0.25, gray) are barely perceptible, so the chart's differentiating feature — edge bundling — is effectively hidden until hover, making the static view indistinguishable from a plain Gantt; 9px task labels across 50 rows push the density boundary and would be unreadable at any reduced viewport size.
